sets.desc: Ethics: the questions you got wrong or asked about in the real Mocks B, C, D, E and F (21 questions), one block per original vignette with only the parts the questions use (word for word). Questions, options and explanations are unchanged.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock B · Paper 1 · Vignette 10

Silva conducts due diligence on a mid-cap packaging company whose stock is actively traded. He determines the company's fundamentals are strong and buys its stock for one of the equity funds he manages. Silva provides commentary on the company's prospects in his monthly client newsletter. Silva has owned the company's stock in his personal portfolio for many years and has disclosed this in the fund's communications to clients. A few weeks after releasing the newsletter, Silva sells some of his personal position in the stock as part of rebalancing his personal portfolio. He earns a substantial profit from this sale.

Tritium's recommended policy for record retention is to maintain records of investment actions and client communications in electronic format. Silva is accustomed to retaining all of his and his clients' relevant files in hard copy form. He does not store any of the records in electronic format. He saves his records for 5 years, after which they are destroyed. Local regulations require record retention for 5 years.

questions.q: Did Silva violate the Standards when selling his personal stake in the packaging company?
options: Yes, because he sold the shares at a profit
Yes, by acting against his own recommendation
questions.why:
A. Correct. Standard VI(B) Priority of Transactions: client transactions have priority. The fund bought first and selling an actively traded stock from his personal portfolio did not disadvantage clients.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: a profit is not a violation as long as clients are not disadvantaged.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the Standard does not prohibit personal transactions that differ from current recommendations as long as clients are not disadvantaged.

questions.q: Does Silva violate the Standards with respect to record retention?
options: Yes, because of the format in which the records are kept
Yes, because records must be retained for a minimum period of 7 years
questions.why:
A. Correct. Standard V(C): records may be kept in hard copy or electronic form, and following the regulatory requirement (5 years) satisfies the Standard; 7 years applies only absent regulation or firm policy.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: the Standard does not require a specific format.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the 7-year recommendation applies only if there is no regulatory requirement; the local rule is 5 years.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock B · Paper 1 · Vignette 11

Murphy's supervisor manages a large research department and, as a result, is not able to personally evaluate the conduct of all the employees in the department. The supervisor hires a deputy manager to oversee several employees and ensures the deputy manager is properly trained. The supervisor establishes the following policies to assist with compliance:

Policy 1: A monetary incentive will be offered as a reward for ethical behavior.

Policy 2: The deputy manager will be responsible for evaluating the ethical conduct of department members.

questions.q: Does Murphy's supervisor violate the Standards in his oversight of the department?
questions.why:
A. Correct. Standard IV(C): incentives (monetary or not) that reward ethical behavior are allowed and delegating supervisory duties in a large department is reasonable.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: monetary incentives for ethical behavior do not violate the Standard.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: delegating supervision to a properly trained deputy is not a violation.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock B · Paper 2 · Vignette 11

During their initial meeting to set up Kagan's account, Dines proposes using Prism's preferred broker to execute trades. Kagan informs Dines that he wishes to trade through another broker that is owned by a friend. Although Dines knows that Prism's preferred broker would provide better execution, without further discussion she agrees to follow Kagan's wishes and use his broker. Additionally, Dines explains that she will not vote any proxies that would not benefit Kagan's account based on a cost-benefit analysis.

At a subsequent meeting, Dines informs Kagan of the premium services offered by her firm at an additional cost, which include direct access to senior research professionals. Kagan decides not to purchase the premium services. A few days later Prism publishes a report changing its recommendation on Cromwell Inc., a cybersecurity company, to a sell. Shortly after publication Dines sets up calls for her premium clients to have detailed discussions with the senior analyst who authored the report, but she does not set up such a call for Kagan. The next day, Kagan calls Dines and asks her to buy Cromwell shares for his account. Dines knows that Kagan is an expert in the cybersecurity sector from their previous interactions. She proceeds to place the order, without informing him of the firm's recent recommendation change.

Several months later, Kagan meets with Dines to discuss how his account has performed relative to other accounts managed with the same strategy. Dines creates a performance presentation that shows the past five years of return data for the top and bottom deciles of all Prism accounts managed with the same strategy. The presentation also includes a disclosure stating that the performance is shown before taxes and gross of fees.

questions.q: Does Dines violate the Standards in the initial meeting with Kagan?
options: Yes, regarding her proxy voting policy
Yes, regarding the broker for Kagan's account
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: Dines violates Standard III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care by not telling Kagan that his directed broker may not give best execution.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: a cost-benefit approach to proxy voting that is disclosed to the client is acceptable.
C. Correct. In a directed brokerage situation the manager must tell the client he may not be getting best execution; Dines did not, violating Standard III(A).

questions.q: Does Dines violate the Standards in her actions related to Cromwell?
options: Yes, because of her actions related to the buy order for Kagan's account
Yes, because of her actions related to setting up calls with the senior analyst
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: Dines violated Standard III(B) Fair Dealing by not telling Kagan about the changed recommendation.
B. Correct. If a client places an order contrary to a current recommendation, the client should be told of the changed recommendation before the order is accepted. Dines did not tell Kagan the rating had changed to sell.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: fair dealing means not equally; premium clients pay for the calls and the calls came after publication, so there is no violation.

questions.q: Dines violates the Standards in her performance presentation for Kagan with regard to:
options: the disclosure of taxes and fees only.
both the account sample and the disclosure of taxes and fees.
questions.why:
A. Correct. Showing only the top and bottom deciles is not fair, accurate and complete (Standard III(D)); a weighted composite of similar portfolios should be used.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: the disclosure that returns are gross of fees and before taxes is adequate.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: only the account sample is a violation; the disclosure is fine.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock C · Paper 1 · Vignette 11

During the first month of BCT's operations, Benoit creates a list of StockCo clients from memory to solicit their business. Benoit then uses an external marketing company to send each prospective client either a card or a coffee mug. She provides this marketing company with a list of clients with their approximate portfolio values. Benoit requests that the company send the coffee mugs to only those clients with portfolios larger than $1 million. During Benoit's employment at StockCo, she had access to the firm's internal data system that contains confidential personal information about StockCo’s clients. The database and its access are managed by Benoit's former department manager at StockCo, Mike Lee, CFA. Lee neglected to remove Benoit's access from the server and, as a result, Benoit discovers that she still has access to the system. Benoit checks the names on the client list that she created from memory against the list in StockCo’s internal data system and confirms that her list is complete and accurate. She then contacts Lee to request him to cancel her access.

questions.q: Who violates the Standard relating to confidentiality during Benoit's first month at BCT?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because both Lee's and Benoit’s actions violate Standard III(E) Preservation of Confidentiality.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because both Lee's and Benoit’s actions violate Standard III(E) Preservation of Confidentiality.
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock C · Paper 2 · Vignette 11

Hirayo will receive a $60,000 performance bonus from Summit if his monthly portfolio performance exceeds that of Summit's other portfolios. He discloses the bonus arrangement to his existing clients but not to prospective clients. Separately, Hirayo will receive a $12,000 reward from Summit after he successfully brought in 20 clients from his previous employer. This reward is paid by Summit and is not charged to clients. Hirayo does not disclose this reward arrangement to the clients that he brought over.

Summit's management team decides to further strengthen its record retention policy. The current policy has the following notable provisions:

Provision 1: Client meeting notes must be preserved in electronic form; hence, any hard copies must be digitized.

Provision 2: Informal blog posts and short message form posts sourced from the internet do not need to be preserved.

Provision 3: Research reports and all supporting documents have a retention period of three years.

questions.q: In relation to his compensation, Hirayo violates the Standards when he fails to disclose:
options: both the $60,000 bonus and the $12,000 reward.
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Hirayo is not in violation of the CFA Institute Code and Standards. The $12,000 does not have to be disclosed to clients because it is not a referral fee or additional compensation, and it does not create a conflict of interest with his employer, clients, or prospective clients.
According to Standard VI(C): Conflicts of Interest, Referral Fees, referral fees are any compensation, consideration, or benefit received from or paid to others for the recommendation of products or services.
The $12,000 reward Hirayo will receive from Summit for bringing over clients from his previous employer is not a referral fee because this reward is paid by Summit (the employer) and not charged to clients. This amount is compensation paid by the firm, not a fee charged to clients.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Hirayo is not in violation of the Standards when he fails to disclose the $12,000 reward received from Summit (the employer) for bringing over clients, with Summit paying the reward that is not charged back to clients. The $12,000 does not have to be disclosed to clients because it is not a referral fee or additional compensation, and it does not create a conflict of interest with his employer, clients, or prospective clients.
However, Hirayo violates the Standards regarding the $60,000 performance bonus arrangement by not disclosing it to his prospective clients.

questions.q: To comply with the Standards, which provision in Summit’s record retention policy should be amended?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because, according to Standard V(C) Record Retention, records may be maintained either in hard copy or electronic form.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because, according to Standard V(C) Record Retention, firms may also implement policies detailing the applicable time frame for retaining research and client communication records. Fulfilling such regulatory and firm requirements satisfies the requirements of Standard V(C).
The Standard adds that in the absence of regulatory guidance or firm policies, CFA Institute recommends maintaining records for at least seven years. The 7-year retention period is only recommended in the absence of a firm policy.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock D · Paper 1 · Vignette 7

While preparing a report on industry trends, Garrett read an article that appeared in a leading business newspaper. Included in the article was a summary of a study conducted by a prominent trade association. Garrett did not obtain a copy of the study directly from the trade association, but did however include information from the article in her report. Garrett cites only the newspaper in her report.

Garrett is part of a working group asked to review IGMA's code of ethics and to suggest any necessary changes that are needed to ensure that it is consistent with the Standards. During one of the working group's discussions, Garrett states that the Standards recommend that the code of ethics include general fiduciary concepts as well as detailed compliance procedures.

questions.q: Did Garrett violate the Standards in her report on industry trends?
options: Yes, because she did not cite the trade association
Yes, because she did not independently review the trade association report
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because in all instances, a member or candidate must cite the actual source of the information. Best practice would be either to obtain the complete study from its original author and cite only that author or to use the information provided by the intermediary and cite both sources. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that the media outlet citation is sufficient.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because there is no requirement that the analyst independently review third-party research. From the reading, in the case of distributing third-party, outsourced research, members and candidates may use and distribute such reports as long as they do not represent themselves as the report’s authors. Indeed, the member or candidate may add value for the client by sifting through research and repackaging it for clients. Therefore, there is no violation of Standard I(C) - Diligence and Reasonable Basis. An unprepared candidate might select this option believing that such reports must be independently reviewed.

questions.q: Is Garrett's statement about the Standard's recommendation for the code of ethics correct?
options: No, with regard to compliance procedures
No, with regard to general fiduciary concepts
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(C) states stand-alone codes of ethics should be written in plain language and should address general fiduciary concepts. They should be unencumbered by numerous detailed procedures. Further, separating the code of ethics from compliance procedures will also reduce, if not eliminate, the legal terminology and boilerplate language that can make the underlying ethical principles incomprehensible to the average person. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that a code of ethics that is compliant with the Standards should include detailed compliance procedures.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the recommended procedures for compliance with Standard IV(C) states stand-alone codes of ethics should be written in plain language and should address general fiduciary concepts. They should be unencumbered by numerous detailed procedures. An unprepared candidate might select this response believing that a code of ethics that is compliant with the Standards should not include general fiduciary concepts.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock E · Paper 1 · Vignette 7

Costa next meets with his largest client. Costa has an arrangement with this client that, if the client's annual portfolio return outperforms its benchmark by more than 5%, Costa gets access to the client’s yacht for three days for personal use. Costa's colleagues are aware of this arrangement, and he has obtained verbal approval from his employer.

questions.q: Does Costa's arrangement with his largest premium client violate the Standard relating to additional compensation arrangements?
options: Yes, because such arrangements are prohibited
Yes, because he did not obtain the appropriate approval
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because, to be consistent with the Standards, Costa is required to obtain written consent from all parties involved to accept the use of the client's yacht. In this case, he received only verbal approval from his employer.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because it would be possible for Costa to enter such an arrangement under the Standards as long as he obtained written consent from all parties involved.
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock E · Paper 2 · Vignette 1

Chan has been working with an internal data science team to develop a machine learning model to improve the bank's forecast of IPO prices. Chan needs to provide a formal recommendation of the model. In its last meeting with Chan, the data science team advised that adding several new variables to the model resulted in a statistically significant increase in forecast accuracy. However, Chan was not clear on how the new variables would improve the accuracy and considers whether to complete the following steps to finalize her recommendation:

Step 1: Review the technical aspects and programming of the model;

Step 2: Review the model factors and parameters to better understand its assumptions and limitations.

Chan receives a call from a client requesting a report on the telecommunications industry. Chan knows that she will not complete a full report because she plans to leave the bank to start her own private equity firm. Chan recalls another partner published a telecommunications industry report last month. However, that partner left the bank shortly after publication and is not available for any follow-up questions. Chan advises the client of the partner's report and forwards it, without changes, to the client.

questions.q: With regard to the machine learning model, to be in compliance with the Standards, Chan must complete:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Step 1, to review the technical aspects and programming of the model, is beyond the requirements of the Standard. Members and candidates are not required to become experts in the technical aspect of the models.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Chan is not required to complete Step 1 to be in compliance with the Standards. Members and candidates are not required to become experts in every technical aspect of the models. Only Step 2 is required to be compliant with the Standards.

questions.q: Did Chan violate the Standards by sending the previously prepared telecommunications industry report to the client?
options: Yes, because the author of the report no longer works at the bank
Yes, because she knowingly provided work completed by another analyst
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because research and models developed while employed by a firm are the property of the firm. The firm retains the right to continue using the work completed after a member or candidate has left the organization.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Chan advises the client of the pre-existing report and shares the report without making any changes or any representations that Chan completed the work herself.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock E · Paper 2 · Vignette 5

Eto's research department releases an updated economic forecast which projects a significant increase in market volatility over the next 12 months. One of Lyden's high-net-worth clients reviews the forecast and expresses concern about the corresponding impact on his portfolio. Lyden suggests the client use a structured product developed by Eto which has a return tied to changes in market volatility. Lyden provides the client with a report describing the basic characteristics and inputs of the product, how it is constructed, and the amount of leverage in the structure. She does not include specific details about the model used to develop the product or details of how inputs were determined. The report only provides the expected performance under an increase in market volatility because that is the client's primary concern.

Lyden is considering adding to the Epic fund's investment in InG Pharma. During a lunch meeting, a well-respected biotech industry analyst tells Lyden that InG Pharma has a promising anti-viral drug in a late-stage drug trial. He believes the drug will come to market in the next 24 months and will significantly increase the company's revenue. Following the conversation, Lyden purchases an additional 50,000 shares of InG for the Epic fund. Lyden shares the analyst's information with a colleague who manages another fund for Eto.

questions.q: Does Lyden violate the Standards in providing the structured product report to her client?
options: Yes, because her report didn't provide specific details about the model or the inputs
Yes, because she should disclose expected performance for both an increase and a decrease in market volatility
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because members and candidates must adequately disclose the general market-related risks and the risks associated with the use of complex financial instruments that are deemed significant. In addition, the member or candidate who prepares the report must include those elements that are important to the analysis and conclusions of the report so that the reader can follow and challenge the report’s reasoning. Lyden's report only discusses performance with an increase in market volatility, not a decrease in market volatility.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the member or candidate who prepares the report must include those elements that are important to the analysis and conclusions of the report so that the reader can follow and challenge the report’s reasoning. A report writer who has done adequate investigation may emphasize certain areas, touch briefly on others, and omit certain aspects deemed unimportant. Lyden included the basic characteristics of the product but doesn't include specific details about the model and the inputs. The specifics of a complex model do not need to be shared.
C. Correct.

questions.q: With regard to InG Pharma, does Lyden violate the Standards regarding material nonpublic information?
options: Yes, because she purchased additional shares for the fund
Yes, because she shared the analyst's information with a colleague
questions.why:
A. Correct. Correct because, according to Standard II(A) regarding material nonpublic information, the information about the drug trial is not material nonpublic information. Lyden is allowed to share the information with a colleague and trade on the information.
In addition to the substance and specificity of the information, the source or relative reliability of the information also determines materiality. The less reliable a source, the less likely the information provided would be considered material. Additionally, information about trials of a new drug, product, or service under development from qualified personnel involved in the trials is likely to be material, whereas educated conjecture by subject experts not connected to the trials is unlikely to be material.
The source of the information is a well-respected industry analyst expressing his opinion on the prospects of the new drug driving InG Pharma's future sales. It is unlikely that his opinion would be considered material.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the information is not material non-public information so she is allowed to purchase shares using this information as an input into her valuation model. 
In addition to the substance and specificity of the information, the source or relative reliability of the information also determines materiality. The less reliable a source, the less likely the information provided would be considered material. Additionally, information about trials of a new drug, product, or service under development from qualified personnel involved in the trials is likely to be material, whereas educated conjecture by subject experts not connected to the trials is unlikely to be material.
The source of the information is a well-respected industry analyst expressing his opinion on the prospects of the new drug driving InG Pharma's future sales. It is unlikely that his opinion would be considered material.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the information is not material non-public information so she is allowed to share it with her research analyst. 
In addition to the substance and specificity of the information, the source or relative reliability of the information also determines materiality. The less reliable a source, the less likely the information provided would be considered material. Additionally, information about trials of a new drug, product, or service under development from qualified personnel involved in the trials is likely to be material, whereas educated conjecture by subject experts not connected to the trials is unlikely to be material.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock F · Paper 1 · Vignette 4

Park receives orders from four of her clients to purchase shares in an oversubscribed IPO. She determines that the IPO is suitable for all of these clients. One of the clients, a family member of Park's, has a regular fee-paying account that is managed similarly to those of the other three clients. Park allocates the shares she receives to the four clients on a pro rata basis according to order size. She discloses the firm's IPO allocation policy to only those clients that participate in IPOs.

questions.q: With regard to her actions associated with the IPO, did Park violate the Standard relating to fair dealing?
options: Yes, because she allocated IPO shares to her family member
Yes, because she did not appropriately disclose the firm's IPO allocation policy
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Park violated Standard III(B) Fair Dealing by not disclosing the trade allocation policy to all clients—she did so to only those clients that participate in IPOs.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Park's allocation of IPO shares to her family member did not violate Standard III(B) Fair Dealing. Because the family member's account is a regular fee-paying account and is managed similarly to other clients' accounts, it was appropriate to allocate IPO shares to the family member.
If the investment professional’s family-member accounts are managed similarly to the accounts of other clients of the firm, however, the family-member accounts should not be excluded from buying such shares.
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock F · Paper 1 · Vignette 7

Fundland plans to offer a structured note to its clients. The structured note replicates the 1-year return of a US equity index, with a 15% cap on upside return and a maximum loss of 15%. Habba sends a brief email to all of her suitable clients with the following two statements and an invitation to follow up if they require more information:

Statement 1: "This note is attractive because, in my view, the market will trend moderately higher."

Statement 2: "This note provides the return of the US equity index with no downside risk."

Both Habba and FundLand are based in Country A. Habba is preparing to market FundLand’s funds to investors in Country B, a rapidly growing economy. Country B investor protection laws are minimal and there are no restrictions on fund distribution and marketing practices. Country A's laws are more restrictive in this regard than the Standards, but Country A laws state that advisory firms must follow the laws of the local country where they conduct business.

questions.q: In her email regarding the structured note, Habba violates the Standards with:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Statement 1 states that Habba is basing her recommendation on her view of the market trend, thereby stating that this is her opinion. Standard V(B)–Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients indicates that the content of any investment recommendation should include the distinction between facts and opinions.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Statement 1 is not a violation as Habba is, in that statement, stating that the market trend is her opinion and not a fact. Standard V(B)–Communication with Clients and Prospective Clients indicates that the content of any investment recommendation should include the distinction between facts and opinions.

questions.q: In marketing the funds in Country B, Habba must follow:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because, although the case states that Country A's laws are more restrictive in this area than the Standards, Country A's laws state that the laws of the location where business is conducted should govern. In this case, the local laws are laws of Country B which are less strict than the Standards.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because, even if the funds are sold in Country B, the Standards are more restrictive than the laws of Country B, and therefore the Standards should govern instead.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock F · Paper 2 · Vignette 5

In a recently published investment report, Li included a table with statistical analysis of publicly available information from a well-recognized industry journal. By downloading the table and not performing the statistical analysis herself, she saved considerable time and effort. Li did not cite the source of the table in her report nor did she verify the statistical analysis.

MCIB's proprietary model predicts that a takeover of Godoggo Corporation is highly likely. In a recent report, Li assigned a "Buy" recommendation to Godoggo's stock. Based on the report, one of MCIB's portfolio managers buys a large number of shares in Godoggo for his fund. He subsequently promotes the stock in several online chat rooms by stating, "I have purchased Godoggo stock because our internal research indicates that it is highly likely to be taken over." A week later, the price of Godoggo's stock has doubled and the portfolio manager subsequently sells all the shares of the stock in his fund.

questions.q: By including the table in her investment report, did Li violate the Standard relating to misrepresentation?
options: Yes, by not citing the source
Yes, by not verifying the statistical analysis
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because Li committed plagiarism by mispresenting the statistical analysis in the table as her own work.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because failing to verify the statistical analysis is not a violation of Standard I(C) - Misrepresentation. Because the statistical analysis table is from a reputable source (a well-recognized industry journal), under Standard V(A) - Diligence and Reasonable Basis, it can reasonably be relied upon without Li having to verify the analysis for herself.
When providing information to clients from a third party, members and candidates share a responsibility for the accuracy of the marketing and distribution materials that pertain to the third party’s capabilities, services, and products.

questions.q: Are the portfolio manager's actions with regard to Godoggo shares a violation of the Standard relating to market manipulation?
options: Yes, because he engaged in transaction-based market manipulation
Yes, because he engaged in information-based market manipulation
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the manager bought the stock based on a recommendation in Li's report and presumably sold the stock because its price had doubled.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the portfolio manager's promotion of the stock was based on a recommendation contained in a report. The portfolio manager was not seemingly attempting to spread false information about the stock.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock B · Paper 1 · Vignette 7

Moreno is tasked with a new project that looks to classify bond issuers based on their probability of default within the next 12 months. He gathers a large sample of financial and accounting metrics for 1,000 issuers and observes that the issuers are not linearly separable. He compares non-linear support vector machine (SVM), unconstrained classification and regression tree (CART), and SVM with soft margin classification. He wants to use a machine-learning algorithm that addresses non-linear separability and is not prone to overfitting.

Moreno also creates Model 1, a logistic regression model that uses two factors, profit margin (PROFIT) and leverage ratio (LEVER), to predict the probability of default. The binary dependent variable is 1 for companies that defaulted within the subsequent 12 months and 0 otherwise. Using the regression results in Exhibit 1, Moreno calculates the predicted probability of default for the average distressed company, which has PROFIT = –2.0 and LEVER = 3.0.

Exhibit 1

# | Coefficient

Intercept | –1.7878

PROFIT | –0.0185

LEVER | 0.3876

To analyze the drivers of ROE for software companies, Moreno collects fundamental data and compares two linear regression models. Model 2 uses profit margin (PROFIT) and interest coverage (COVER). Model 3 extends Model 2 by adding a third factor, the quick ratio (QUICK).

Exhibit 2

# | Coefficient | t-Statistic | p-Value

Intercept | –1.4411 | –3.4888 | 0.0000

PROFIT | 0.4840 | 49.5319 | 0.0000

COVER | 0.7487 | 27.9215 | 0.0000

QUICK | 0.0919 | 1.9204 | 0.0558

Finally, Moreno wants to test if last-12-month sales (SALES) are a good predictor of ROE. He runs Model 4, which has the following specification:

A plot of the regression residuals against SALES is presented in Exhibit 3.

Note: Exhibit 3 was an image in the original paper (file KL3.png) and was not in the pasted text. From the answer explanation: in the plot of the Model 4 residuals against SALES, the variance of the residuals increases as SALES increase.

questions.q: Which of the following machine-learning algorithms is most suitable for Moreno's bond issuer classification model?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: non-linear SVM with more advanced boundaries reduces training misclassifications but is complex and prone to overfitting.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: unconstrained CART can perfectly learn the training data and overfit unless regularization parameters are added.
C. Correct. SVM with soft margin classification adds a penalty for misclassified training observations and trades off a wider margin against total error, handling non-linear separability without overfitting.

questions.q: For the average distressed company, the probability of default predicted by Model 1 is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct. P = 1/[1 + exp(−(−1.7878 − 0.0185 × (−2.0) + 0.3876 × 3.0))] = 1/(1 + 1.8004) = 0.357, about 36%.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: 0.56 is exp(b0 + b1PROFIT + b2LEVER) = exp(−0.5880), the odds, not the probability.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: 77% omits the intercept.

questions.q: Compared to Model 2, Model 3 most likely has a:
options: lower R-squared and a higher adjusted R-squared.
higher R-squared and a lower adjusted R-squared.
higher R-squared and a higher adjusted R-squared.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: R² never decreases when a variable is added.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: adjusted R² rises when the added coefficient's |t| > 1.0, and QUICK's t-statistic is 1.9204.
C. Correct. R² increases or stays the same when a variable is added, and adjusted R² increases if the new coefficient's |t-statistic| is above 1.0 (QUICK: 1.9204).

questions.q: The most appropriate conclusion to draw from the residual plot for Model 4 is that:
options: the model suffers from unconditional heteroskedasticity.
there is a non-linear relationship between ROE and SALES.
the F-test for the overall regression significance is unreliable.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: the residual variance increases with SALES, so it is correlated with an independent variable: conditional, not unconditional, heteroskedasticity.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: a residual plot does not show the form of the relationship between target and feature.
C. Correct. With conditional heteroskedasticity the MSE is a biased estimator, so the F-test for overall significance is unreliable (and Type I errors rise).

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock B · Paper 2 · Vignette 2

Danny Aoun is an equity portfolio manager at Betterflow Investments. He is developing sentiment indicators for forecasting stock price movements. Aoun gathers textual data from the internet to build machine-learning models. He extracts raw content from a variety of online sources and then trains the models for sentiment prediction. Each text item is labelled as either positive sentiment or negative sentiment. Aoun is more concerned about the models producing false negatives than false positives. He computes selected performance metrics for three models using confusion matrices and presents the metrics in Exhibit 1.

Exhibit 1

# Model | Precision | Recall | F1 Score | Accuracy

X | 0.87 | 0.94 | 0.90 | 0.88

Y | 0.93 | 0.90 | 0.91 | 0.92

Z | 0.96 | 0.82 | 0.88 | 0.86

For Bytewave, Aoun estimates a first-order autoregressive model (AR(1)) on the stock price. From the results, he concludes that the time-series model exhibits autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity and has ARCH(1) errors.

questions.q: Which machine-learning model should Aoun choose given his concern about false negatives?
questions.why:
A. Correct. Recall (correctly predicted positives / all actual positives) is the metric to use when false negatives are costly. Model X has the highest recall (0.94).
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: Model Y has the highest accuracy and F1 score, which weight false positives and false negatives equally.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: Model Z has the highest precision, which matters when false positives are costly.

questions.q: Based on Aoun's conclusion regarding the time-series model for Bytewave, the variance of the error term is:
questions.why:
A. Correct. With ARCH(1) errors the variance in period t + 1 depends on the squared error of period t, so it is not constant but predictable.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: ARCH errors have a non-constant variance.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: ARCH(1) makes the variance depend linearly on the previous squared error, so it is predictable.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock C · Paper 1 · Vignette 9

Helmer also builds a logistic regression model to predict the 1-year probability of default for junk bond issuers. She collects data for 70 issuers over the past five years and identifies those that defaulted within the subsequent year (DEFAULT = 1) and those that did not default (DEFAULT = 0). She uses two independent variables in the logistic regression model: the ratio of debt to total capital (LEVERAGE) and the interest coverage ratio (COVERAGE). The coefficients of the regression are shown in Exhibit 1. Using this model, Helmer then estimates the probability of default by ACME, an issuer with LEVERAGE of 0.8 and COVERAGE of 0.9.

Exhibit 1

#  | Coefficient

Intercept | –20.0

LEVERAGE | 65.5

COVERAGE | –35.0

Helmer assesses possible violations of regression assumptions in Model 1 and makes the following observations:

Observation 1: There are significant deviations of the residuals from the diagonal in the Q-Q plot.

Observation 2: The null hypothesis of the Breusch–Pagan test is rejected.

questions.q: Based on the logistic regression model, the probability that ACME defaults within the next year is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the negative sign is omitted when calculating the event probability. The event probability is incorrectly calculated as:
P = 1/(1 + exp(b0 + b1 × LEVERAGE + b2 × COVERAGE)).
Based on the coefficient estimates in Exhibit 1 and the value of the independent variables for ACME:
P = 1/(1 + exp(–20 + 65.5 × 0.8 – 35 × 0.9)) = 1/(1 + exp(0.9)) = 0.2891 or 29%
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the regression is treated as a linear regression instead of a logistic regression and the probability of default is incorrectly calculated as:
P = b0 + b1 × LEVERAGE + b2 × COVERAGE
P = –20 + 65.5 × 0.8 – 35 × 0.9 = 0.9 or 90%
In case the intercept is missed in calculating the event probability in the logistic regression model, the default probability is 100%, which is closest to 90%.
The event probability is incorrectly calculated as:
P = 1/(1 + exp(–(b1 × LEVERAGE + b2 × COVERAGE))).
Based on the coefficient estimates in Exhibit 1 and the value of the independent variables for ACME:
P = 1/(1 + exp(–(65.5 × 0.8 – 35 × 0.9))) = 1/(1 + exp(–20.9)) = 1.0000 or 100%

questions.q: Observation 1 indicates a violation of which regression assumption?
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because a Q-Q plot is used to visualize the distribution of a variable by comparing it to a normal distribution (the diagonal). Significant deviations of the residuals from the diagonal of the Q-Q plot, as per Observation 1, indicate that the residuals are not normally distributed, but it does not mean that there is heteroskedasticity. Homoskedasticity could be visually explored with a scatterplot between dependent and independent variables included in the regression.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because a Q-Q plot is used to visualize the distribution of a variable by comparing it to a normal distribution (the diagonal). The Q-Q plot cannot be used to identify non-linear relationships between the dependent variable (Y) and the independent variables (Xi). Significant deviations of the residuals from the diagonal of the Q-Q plot, as per Observation 1, indicate that the residuals are not normally distributed, but this does not mean that there is interdependence of explanatory variables or multicollinearity. A pairwise scatterplot of the independent variables is used to detect this relationship.

Source: Mock F · Paper 1 · Vignette 8

Hardie uses the models to determine the mean-reverting level of NTPC. He also forecasts NTPC for the next two weeks given that it is 0.061 in the current week and was 0.034 in the prior week. He then uses the regression statistics in Exhibit 1 to compare the forecasting performance of the two models.

Exhibit 1

#  | AR(1) Model | AR(2) Model

R-squared | 0.907 | 0.905

Standard error of regression | 0.027 | 0.027

Root mean squared error | 0.032 | 0.030

questions.q: Compared to the AR(1) model, the out-of-sample forecasting performance of the AR(2) model is:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because we compare the out-of-sample forecasting performance of forecasting models by comparing their root mean squared error (RMSE). The model with the smallest RMSE is judged the most accurate, and not the model with the largest R-squared. This means that the AR(2) model has better out-of-sample forecasting performance.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because we compare the out-of-sample forecasting performance of forecasting models by comparing their root mean squared error (RMSE), and not the standard error of regression. The model with the smallest RMSE is judged the most accurate, which means that the AR(2) model has better out-of-sample forecasting performance.
C. Correct.

Source: Mock F · Paper 2 · Vignette 9

Kendall gathers the model output for silver returns and tests whether the model explains RET with any statistical significance. She uses the partial ANOVA table results in Exhibit 1 and notes that the critical value of the F-statistic is 3.813 at the 1% significance level and 2.619 at the 5% significance level.

Exhibit 1

# Source | Degrees of Freedom | Sum of Squares | Mean Squares

Regression | 3 | 0.0453 | 0.0151

questions.q: Do the independent variables jointly contribute to the explanation of silver returns?
options: Yes, at the 5% significance level only
Yes, at both the 5% and 1% significance levels
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the joint contribution is tested using the F-statistic for the overall model. The F-statistic is calculated as F = mean square regression / mean square error = MSR/MSE = 0.0151/0.0015 ≈ 10. This exceeds the critical value at the 5% and 1% significance levels. 
This response would be chosen if F were calculated as mean square error / mean square regression = MSE/MSR = 0.0015/0.0151 ≈ 0.1.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the joint contribution is tested using the F-statistic for the overall model. The F-statistic is calculated as F = mean square regression / mean square error = MSR/MSE = 0.0151/0.0015 ≈ 10. This exceeds the critical value at the 5% and 1% significance levels. 
This response would be chosen if F were calculated as sum of squares regression / mean square regression = SSR/MSR = 0.0453/0.0151 = 3.
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock B · Paper 2 · Vignette 3

Team Green is asked to discuss how investment in physical capital, human capital, and technological development affects economic growth. As a summary of the discussion, Team Green presents a number of points including the following three:

Point 1: Since technology results in an upward shift in the production function, the relationship between economic growth and R&D spending is positive in the short run.

Point 2: Total factor productivity reflects the state of technology, and can be measured by the contribution of capital deepening plus the growth rates of labor productivity.

Point 3: Although long-term sustainable growth cannot rely on pure capital deepening, the impact of investment spending on available capital depends on the existing physical capital stock.

Team Purple is asked to investigate whether the per capita income of a developing country should converge toward that of developed countries over time. Team Purple reviews various determinants of per capital incomes: saving rate, population growth rate, the shape of production function, and the externalities associated with human capital. After a debate among team members, Team Purple concludes that the externalities associated with human capital is the most important determinant in predicting the occurrence of convergence.

Smith presents the expected impact of removing trade barriers to economic growth. Referring to the neoclassical growth model, Smith concludes that opening up the economy should increase the rate at which countries' capital-to-labor ratios converge. Team Orange is asked to describe the dynamic adjustment process consistent with Smith's conclusion. Team Orange provides the following descriptions:

Description 1: The growth in the capital-exporting countries will be above the steady state.

Description 2: Developed countries will tend to run trade deficits as they export capital.

Description 3: The rate of return on investments will be lower in countries with high capital-to-labor ratios.

questions.q: Which of the points raised by Team Green is most likely correct?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: the relationship between R&D spending and growth is not clear-cut in the short run (creative destruction can slow growth cyclically).
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: labor productivity growth equals the contribution of capital deepening plus TFP growth, so TFP is not capital deepening plus labor productivity growth.
C. Correct. The impact of investment on available capital depends on the existing capital stock (large in developing countries), even though sustainable long-term growth cannot rely on capital deepening alone.

questions.q: Which of the following convergence concepts is most compatible with Team Purple's conclusion?
questions.why:
A. Correct. Externalities from human capital (endogenous growth) remove diminishing returns, so rich countries can keep their lead; the model makes no prediction that convergence occurs.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: absolute convergence assumes diminishing marginal returns to capital and the same technology.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: conditional convergence also assumes diminishing returns to capital (the neoclassical model).

questions.q: Which of the following descriptions provided by Team Orange is consistent with Smith's conclusion?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: growth in the capital-exporting countries will be below the steady state (capital flows out to the capital-poor country).
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: capital-poor countries run trade deficits while developed countries run trade surpluses as they export capital.
C. Correct. Marginal product of capital is lower where capital per worker is high, so returns are lower in high capital-to-labor countries and higher in low capital-to-labor countries.

Source: Mock C · Paper 1 · Vignette 1

One year ago, Kuspa hedged the currency risk of a Australian dollar (AUD) 50,000,000 long position by selling AUD one year forward at an all-in forward price of 0.7530 USD/AUD (0.7530 USD per 1 AUD). Now, nine months before the forward's settlement date, Kuspa marks the forward position to market based on the data in Exhibit 1 (MRR is the market reference rate).

Exhibit 1

Exchange Rate Data (USD/AUD)

# Maturity | Bid | Offer

Spot | 0.7233 | 0.7234

9 months (forward points) | +7 | +8

Other Data

# Interest Rate | US | Australia

MRR (annual rate) | 0.28% | 0.10%

Finally, Kuspa analyzes the risks related to the currencies of three emerging market countries, summarized in Exhibit 3. These countries have recently experienced increased global investor interest and significant foreign capital inflows. Kuspa uses the information in Exhibit 3 to evaluate the potential negative effects of these inflows.

Exhibit 3

# Risk Characteristic | Country D | Country E | Country F

Equity market returns (5-year compound annual growth rate) | 20% | 7% | 19%

External debt (% of GDP) | 120% | 60% | 300%

Foreign exchange reserves (% average daily foreign exchange turnover in domestic currency) | 27% | 30% | 30%

questions.q: The mark-to-market value (in USD) of the USD/AUD forward position is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because it is the undiscounted net cash inflow.
50,000,000 × (0.753 – 0.7234) = 1,440,000
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because it is based on the bid quotes rather than the offer quotes in Exhibit 1. Using bids, the all-in forward price is 0.7233 + 0.0007 = 0.7240, the offsetting transaction using this incorrect rate is (AUD 50,000,000)(0.7240 USD/AUD) = USD 36,200,000, resulting in a net cash inflow of USD 37,650,000 − USD 36,200,000 = USD 1,450,000 which, in present value terms, is (USD 1,450,000)/[1 + (0.28%)(0.750)] = USD 1,446,961.

questions.q: Based on Kuspa's risk analysis, which emerging market country is least exposed to the potential negative effects of the foreign capital inflows?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because compared to Country E (1) Country D's higher asset price growth (20% 5-year compound growth rate versus 7% for Country E) means Country D is more likely to enter or be in an asset bubble related to foreign capital chasing high returns; and (2) Country D's level of external debt as a % of GDP is twice as large as Country E's, indicating a greater risk of the potential bad effects of running large current account deficits (e.g., deteriorating terms of trade may be associated with currency crises).
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because its 19% compound asset price growth and 300% ratio of external debt to GDP are factors increasing the likelihood that Country F may impose capital controls compared to Country E, while its level of foreign exchange reserves (matching Country E's) gives Country F no preference over Country E.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock C · Paper 2 · Vignette 2

Country A has a developed, slow-growing economy and a high rate of capital per worker. Exhibit 1 provides the average annual growth rates for selected economic variables in Country A over the most recent five years. Simpson uses this information to determine the contribution of capital deepening to factor productivity.

Exhibit 1

Hours worked | 0.6%

Labor productivity | 1.4%

Total factor productivity | 0.5%

Country B's potential GDP currently exceeds its actual GDP. Simpson forecasts that Country B's potential GDP growth rate will be higher than the actual GDP growth rate over the next two years. She assesses the implications of her forecast on Country B's economy.

questions.q: Which of the following policies would most likely have the greatest impact on economic growth in Country A?
options: Loosening credit restraints in the financial sector
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because Country A is a developed country with a high rate of capital per worker. Consequently, increased savings and investment, which would further increase capital per worker, is unlikely to substantially increase economic growth.
One of the major problems for some developing countries is a low level of capital per worker.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because Country A being a developed economy already has a high rate of capital per worker and the economy is growing slowly. Consequently, a loosening of credit restraints, which would encourage additional capital, is unlikely to substantially increase economic growth.

questions.q: In the most recent five years, the contribution of capital deepening to Country A's labor productivity growth was:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is the difference between the labor productivity annual growth rate and the growth rates of hours worked and total factor productivity:
1.4% – 0.6% – 0.5% = 0.3%
The contribution of capital deepening to Country A's labor productivity growth should be the difference between the labor productivity growth rate and the total factor productivity growth rate:
= 1.4% – 0.5% = 0.9%
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because this is the difference between the labor productivity growth rate and the growth rate of the hours worked:
= 1.4% – 0.6% = 0.8%
The contribution of capital deepening to Country A's labor productivity growth should be the difference between the labor productivity growth rate and the total factor productivity growth rate:
= 1.4% – 0.5% = 0.9%
C. Correct.

questions.q: Simpson's forecast for Country B's GDP growth rate implies that inflationary pressures will most likely:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because actual GDP growth above (below) the potential GDP growth rate puts upward (downward) pressure on inflation.
Since Country B's actual GDP growth rate is presently lower than its potential GDP growth rate, and because this is also forecasted to continue in the future, there will likely be downward pressure on inflation.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because actual GDP growth above (below) the potential GDP growth rate puts upward (downward) pressure on inflation.
Since Country B's actual GDP growth rate is presently lower than its potential GDP growth rate, and because this is also forecasted to continue in the future, there will likely be downward pressure on inflation.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock D · Paper 1 · Vignette 9

Nine months ago, Podowski bought EUR 20 million forward against the USD by entering into a 1-year forward contract at 1.1308 USD/EUR. He wants to calculate the mark-to-market value of this position today. The current USD/EUR spot rate is quoted at 1.1352/1.1355 and the 90-day forward points are –14/–12. The annualized 90-day market reference rate (Actual/360) is 0.53% for USD and 0.77% for EUR.

Francis is looking for potential carry trades to recommend to her clients. She focuses on a potential trade between the AUD and the South African rand (ZAR). She reviews what market conditions are required for the trade to be profitable.

questions.q: The mark-to-market value of Podowski's USD/EUR forward contract is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the offer, and not the bid, is used for the offsetting contract. The all-in offer rate is 1.1355 – 12/10,000 = 1.1343 USD/EUR.
EUR 20 million × 1.1343 USD/EUR = USD 22,686,000. This gives a positive cash flow of USD 70,000 (22,686,000 – 22,616,000). Discounted at the 90-day MRR, the PV equals:
USD 70,000 / [1 + 0.0053(90/360)] = USD 69,907.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the forward points are subtracted, which gives an all-in bid rate of 1.1352 – (–14/10,000) = 1.1366 USD/EUR. 
On settlement, Podowski will pay USD 22,616,000 (20,000,000 × 1.1308) on the original forward and receive USD 22,732,000 (20,000,000 × 1.1366) from the offsetting forward, resulting in a positive cash flow of USD 116,000 (22,732,000 – 22,616,000). Discounted at the 90-day MRR, the PV equals:
USD 116,000 / [1 + 0.0053(90/360)] = USD 115,847.

questions.q: What condition would best support Francis' trade proposal between AUD and ZAR?
options: Covered interest rate parity not holding in the short term
The interest rate differential between the two countries being expected to widen after the trade is initiated
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because for a carry trade to succeed, it is uncovered interest rate parity, not covered interest rate parity, that must not hold. If it held, the investor would receive identical returns from either an unhedged foreign currency return or a domestic currency investment as the appreciation or depreciation of the exchange rate would offset the yield differential. If uncovered interest rate parity held at all times, investors would not be able to profit from a strategy that undertook long positions in high-yield currencies and short positions in low-yield currencies. The change in spot rates over the tenor of the forward contracts would cancel out the interest rate differentials locked in at the inception of the position.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the difference in yields is locked in at the time of the trade, so the movement of the yield spread once the trade is initiated is irrelevant.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock E · Paper 2 · Vignette 10

Country A is a developing economy and its population growth rate will continue to be higher than that in developed economies. Country A's long-term goal is to accelerate economic growth so that its level of per capita income will eventually match that of developed economies. Country A intends to implement trade policies and develop legal, political, and economic institutions of developed countries to support this goal.

Ling intends to trade government bonds issued by Country A and Country B. Ling's outlook is that Country A's actual GDP growth rate will stay above the potential GDP growth rate and that Country B will experience much lower inflation than the current market forecast.

questions.q: The type of convergence occurring if Country A achieves its long-term goal is best referred to as:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because absolute convergence means that developing countries, regardless of their particular characteristics, will eventually catch up with the developed countries and match them in per capita output, whereas Ling believes Country A will converge if it introduces trade policies and successfully develops its legal, political, and economic institutions to support this goal. Furthermore, absolute convergence implies convergence of per capita growth rates among all countries. It does not, however, imply that the level of per capita income will be the same in all countries, whereas Country A plans to achieve the same income level of developed countries.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because conditional convergence means that convergence is conditional on the countries having the same saving rate, population growth rate, and production function. Country A has higher population growth than developed economies.

questions.q: Based on Ling's outlook, which country's bonds would most likely increase in price?
options: Both Country A's bonds and Country B's bonds
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because actual GDP growth above (below) the potential GDP growth rate puts upward (downward) pressure on inflation, which puts corresponding pressure on nominal interest rates and bond prices. Ling expects Country A's actual GDP growth rate will stay above the potential GDP growth rate. This leads to higher inflation and lower, not higher, bond prices.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because actual GDP growth above (below) the potential GDP growth rate puts upward (downward) pressure on inflation, which puts corresponding pressure on nominal interest rates and bond prices. Ling expects Country B will experience much lower inflation than the current market forecast. This leads to higher bond prices for Country B. Ling expects Country A's actual GDP growth rate will stay above the potential GDP growth rate. This leads to higher inflation and lower, not higher, bond prices.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock F · Paper 1 · Vignette 9

Nod reviews the information on three developing economies in Exhibit 3. There are no material differences in the countries' saving rates, population growth rates, and production functions. Nod believes that the three countries will benefit from conditional convergence with developed economies.

Exhibit 3

#  | Country B | Country C | Country D

Capital-to-labor ratio | 40% | 40% | 30%

Per capita income | $1,100 | $1,000 | $1,000

questions.q: Assuming conditional convergence, which country is most likely to experience the highest growth in per capita income?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the capital-to-labor ratio for Country B is higher than that for Country D and, as per conditional convergence, the economy with a lower capital-to-labor ratio will experience more rapid growth of productivity and per capita income.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because, even though Country C's per capita income is the same as Country D's, the capital-to-labor ratio for Country C is higher than that for Country D and, as per conditional convergence, the economy with a lower capital-to-labor ratio will experience more rapid growth of productivity and per capita income.
C. Correct.

vignettes.body:
Source: Mock F · Paper 2 · Vignette 2

Chun Tian is a US-based portfolio manager actively involved in the foreign exchange market.

Three months ago, Tian made a 6-month deposit of 50 million Australian dollars (AUD) at the annualized 6-month AUD reference interest rate. She then fully hedged the deposit by selling AUD forward against USD. Today, she marks the forward position to market and notes that reference rates have not changed over the past three months. Selected current reference rates are provided in Exhibit 1.

Exhibit 1

#  | 3-Month | 6-Month

AUD reference rate (annualized) | 0.60% | 0.67%

USD reference rate (annualized) | 0.26% | 0.36%

questions.q: Assuming covered interest rate parity holds, the all-in annualized USD return that Tian should earn on the AUD deposit is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because 0.26% is the 3-month annualized USD reference rate, but the AUD deposit has a term of 6 months. Candidates who mix up the time duration of placement and maturity of the deposit, but do not overlook the fact that the question asks for the rate of return in USD terms, may incorrectly select this answer option.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because 0.67% is the 6-month annualized AUD reference rate. Candidates who overlook the fact that the question asks for the rate of return in USD terms may incorrectly select this answer option.

Source: Mock B · Paper 1 · Vignette 2

On 1 January of the current year, Lonza granted 4 million stock options to employees. The options vest 3 years after the grant date and expire 6 years after the grant date. The fair value per option was EUR 1.8 on the grant date.

Exhibit 2

# | Most Recent Year | Prior Year

Liquidity Coverage Ratio | 95% | 110%

Net Stable Funding Ratio | 95% | 90%

questions.q: For the current year, Lonza's compensation expense related to its stock options will be:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: this divides the total fair value by the 6-year term to expiry instead of the vesting period.
B. Correct. Expense = (4 million × EUR 1.8) / 3-year vesting period = EUR 2.4 million.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: this recognizes the whole grant-date fair value in one year, without spreading it over the vesting period.

questions.q: Based on Lonza's liquidity ratios at the end of the most recent year, which of the following is correct?
options: Lonza's Net Stable Funding Ratio has deteriorated from the prior year
Lonza's required stable funding is higher than its available stable funding
Lonza can withstand cash outflows 5% higher than its 30-day liquidity needs in a stress scenario
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: a higher NSFR is an improvement and it rose from 90% to 95%.
B. Correct. NSFR = available stable funding / required stable funding. At 95% (below 100%), required stable funding is higher than available stable funding.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: an LCR of 95% means Lonza can cover only 95% of its 30-day stress outflows, i.e. 5% less, not 5% more.

questions.q: The market with the highest sustainable sales growth rate is:

A. Incorrect. Incorrect: Thailand's organic growth is only 5% + 0% = 5%; 4% came from exchange rates, which is less sustainable.
B. Correct. Sustainable growth comes from volume and price, not exchange rates. Malaysia: 4% + 5% = 9%, above Thailand (5%) and Hong Kong SAR (−4% + 8% = 4%).

questions.q: Which of the following ratios for Creamy most likely remains unchanged after translation for the most recent year?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: current assets include inventory translated at the historical rate (14,700) and monetary items at the year-end rate (14,000), while liabilities are at 14,000, so the ratio changes.
B. Correct. Under the temporal method sales are translated at the average rate and COGS at the rate when the inventory was purchased; both are 14,700, so the translated ratio equals the local-currency ratio.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: sales use the average rate (14,700) and receivables the year-end rate (14,000), so the ratio changes.

Option 1: Borrow directly against the receivables of EUR 50 million;

Option 2: Create a special purpose entity (SPE), invest EUR 10 million in the SPE, have the SPE borrow EUR 40 million, and then use the funds to purchase EUR 50 million of receivables from Acme.

McAndrew considers the potential impact of these options on Acme's consolidated debt-to-assets ratio, assuming that Acme will be able to influence the financial and operating policy of the SPE, and will be expected to absorb any losses that the SPE may incur.

questions.q: Acme's consolidated debt-to-assets ratio would most likely be:
options: lower under Option 1 compared to Option 2.
the same under either Option 1 or Option 2.
higher under Option 1 compared to Option 2.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: Acme controls the SPE (influence over policies and exposure to variable returns), so it consolidates it and the balance sheet looks the same as borrowing directly.
B. Correct. Under IFRS 10 / SIC-12, control (influence over financial and operating policy and exposure to variable returns) requires consolidation, so the consolidated ratio is the same under both options.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: consolidation makes the two options identical on the balance sheet.

Half of the excess was attributable to Begonia's plant and equipment, and the other half was attributable to land. RMRL has the ability to exercise significant influence over Begonia. Ahmad expects Begonia to report net income of $1,500,000 for the current year and not pay any dividends. Ahmad assumes Begonia does not have any intercompany transactions with RMRL. He then estimates the carrying value of RMRL's investment in Begonia at the end of the current year.

Ahmad reviews the trend in RMRL's balance-sheet-based and cash-flow-based accruals ratios, as well as the trend in the Beneish M-scores and Altman Z-scores over the past two years, using the data in Exhibit 1.

Exhibit 1

Cash-flow-based accruals ratio | 1.7% | –2.5%

questions.q: The estimated carrying value for RMRL's investment in Begonia at the end of the current year should be:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because this calculation does not account for the annual amortization of the excess purchase price attributable to Begonia's plant and equipment:
= $12,000,00 + (30% × $1,500,000)
= $12,450,000
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because this calculation includes 100% of Begonia's net income instead of RMRL's 30% share of Begonia's net income:
= $12,000,000 + $1,500,000 – $107,500

questions.q: With respect to RMRL's accruals ratios, Ahmad should conclude that
options: both the balance-sheet-based accruals ratio and the cash-flow-based accruals ratio have improved.
the balance-sheet-based accruals ratio has deteriorated, but the cash-flow-based accruals ratio has improved.
the balance-sheet-based accruals ratio has improved, but the cash-flow-based accruals ratio has deteriorated.

Source: Mock D · Paper 1 · Vignette 6

Delphine recently announced that it would be increasing its ownership interest in Company A from 35% to 50%. Delphine and Company A are both profitable. Kriser considers how Delphine's net profit margin might be affected after the increase in ownership under the following scenarios:

Scenario 1: Delphine exercises significant influence, but not control, over Company A.

Scenario 2: Delphine exercises control over Company A.

Kriser is concerned that recent industry changes may negatively affect one of Delphine's cash-generating units. She evaluates the following projections to determine the expected impairment loss under IFRS:

Carrying value of cash-generating unit: €18,200,000

Recoverable amount of cash-generating unit: €17,700,000

Goodwill allocated to cash-generating unit: €300,000

questions.q: Delphine's net profit margin under Scenario 1 would be:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because sales would be higher under Scenario 2, while net income would be the same under Scenario 1 and Scenario 2, making net profit margin (net income / sales) higher under Scenario 1. This answer incorrectly assumes that sales is the same under both scenarios but that net income is higher under consolidation (Scenario 2), or that net income is the same under both scenarios but that sales is lower under Scenario 2.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because sales would be higher under Scenario 2, while net income would be the same under Scenario 1 and Scenario 2, making net profit margin (net income / sales) higher under Scenario 1. This answer incorrectly assumes that the equity method (Scenario 1) and consolidation (Scenario 2) have the same effect on net income and sales.
C. Correct.

questions.q: Based on Kriser's projections, the expected impairment loss for Delphine's cash-generating unit is:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because the impairment loss under IFRS is the difference between the recoverable amount and the carrying value of the cash-generating unit. This answer choice assumes that the impairment loss is the difference between the excess carrying value and the recorded goodwill of the cash-generating unit.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because the impairment loss (the difference between these two amounts) is first applied to the goodwill that has been allocated to the cash-generating unit. Once this has been reduced to zero, the remaining amount of the loss is then allocated to all of the other non-cash assets in the unit on a pro rata basis. This answer choice assumes that the impairment loss is limited to the goodwill allocated to the reporting unit.
C. Correct.

Source: Mock D · Paper 2 · Vignette 11

Carter first considers Gowran's capital adequacy. For the most recent year end, Gowran reported Common Equity Tier 1 Capital of $15 billion and risk-weighted assets of $100 billion. Carter determines Gowran's pro forma year-end Common Equity Tier 1 Capital ratio to account for the following two events, which occurred after the most recent year end.

Gowran issued $1 billion of Additional Tier 1 Capital.

The regulator required Gowran to recognize an additional $3.5 billion of operational risk-weighted assets.

Carter next assesses Gowran's asset quality by analyzing the adequacy of its allowance for loan losses. Specifically, he examines how the ratio of the bank's allowance for loan losses to non-performing loans changed during the most recent year based on the data (in millions) in Exhibit 1.

Exhibit 1

Non-performing loans at start of year | $2,000

Non-performing loans at end of year | $2,400

Allowance for loan losses at start of year | $1,500

Provision for loan losses during the year | $500

Charge-offs, net of recoveries, during the year | $200

As part of its executive management compensation, Gowran also has a stock option plan (Plan B). Three years ago, Gowran granted executives 5 million at-the-money stock options with a three-year vesting period. On the grant date, Gowran's share price was $12 and the fair value of each option was $3. All of the options are now vested in the current year. Carter determines the effect on Gowran's paid-in capital on its balance sheet in the current year, assuming that 2 million of the stock options are exercised at the strike price of $12 and Gowran's share price is currently $18.

questions.q: Gowran's pro forma Common Equity Tier 1 Capital ratio is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect because this indicates that neither of the actions that occurred after year end affected the Common Equity Tier 1 Capital Ratio (i.e., $15 billion / $100 billion = 15.0%)
While the issuance of Additional Tier 1 Capital is correctly excluded from the Common Equity Tier 1 Capital Ratio, the additional operational risk-weighted assets should be included. The latter might be assumed to be true if the only type of risk-weighted assets related to credit risk and while it is typically the largest component of risk-weighted assets for a bank, it is not the only type.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because this would be the pro forma Common Equity Tier 1 Capital ratio at year end for Gowran if both actions occurring after year end were assumed to have an effect on the ratio as follows: ($15 billion + $1 billion) / ($100 billion + $3.5 billion) = 15.46% ~ 15.5%.

questions.q: Over the most recent year, the ratio of Gowran's allowances for loan losses to non-performing loans:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because over the past year, the ratio of Gowran's allowances for loan losses to non-performing loans did not change. 
The conclusion that the ratio decreased could be derived if provision for loan losses during the year was subtracted rather than added when calculating the allowance for loan losses at the end of the year.
Allowance for loan losses at start of year	1,500
Subtract: Provision for loan losses during the year	500
Subtract: Net charge-offs during the year	200
Allowance for loan losses at end of year	800
Then the calculation of the ratio of allowances for loan losses to non-performing loans becomes;
 	Start of Year	End of Year
Allowances for loan losses	1,500	800
Non-performing loans	2,000	2,400
Ratio	0.75	0.33
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because over the past year, the ratio of Gowran's allowances for loan losses to non-performing loans did not change. 
The conclusion that the ratio increased could be derived if the net charge-offs were added rather than subtracted in calculating the allowance for loan losses at the end of the year.
Allowance for loan losses at start of year	1,500
Add: Provision for loan losses during the year	500
Add: Net charge-offs during the year	200
Allowance for loan losses at end of year	2,200
Then the calculation of the ratio of allowances for loan losses to non-performing loans becomes;
 	Start of Year	End of Year
Allowances for loan losses	1,500	2,200
Non-performing loans	2,000	2,400
Ratio	0.75	0.92

questions.q: Based on Carter's assumptions regarding the exercise of the share options, paid-in capital on Gowran's balance sheet in the current year will increase by:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this ignores the $6 million transferred from share-based compensation reserve to paid-in capital and only considers the $24 million amount which is 2 million options at $12 strike price.
B. Correct.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect because the adjustment to paid-in capital is incorrectly calculated as a $36 million increase which is based on 2 million options exercised at the current share price of $18 (rather than using the strike price of $12) plus the $6 million transferred from share-based compensation reserve.

As part of her analysis, McCabe uses the CAMELS (capital adequacy, asset quality, management, earnings, liquidity, and sensitivity) approach. She reviews Acme's selected financial information (in $ millions) for the most recent year in Exhibit 1 and computes its Common Equity Tier 1 Capital Ratio.

A. Incorrect. Incorrect because this calculation uses total book assets (instead of risk-weighted assets):
(Common stockholders' equity – Intangible assets – Deferred tax assets) / Total book assets = (176,400 – 18,784 – 7,986)/1,596,723 = 0.0937107 ≈ 9%.

Common stockholders' equity / Total risk-weighted assets = 176,400/1,042,361 = 0.1692312 ≈ 17%.
